verdict.summary: You can create an app and connect your own account quickly, with no review. Distribution outside the Marketplace is capped (10 accounts private, 25 installs for marketplace-distribution apps) until a Marketplace listing is approved. Certification is a further, much longer step.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours to connect; 1-3 days to prepare a Marketplace listing
verdict.approval_wait: None to connect your own account or a few invited accounts; listing initial review is 10 business days (HubSpot-documented)

gates.name: Developer account app, install in your own account
gates.unlocks: You create the app and install it into your own HubSpot account via the install URL.
limits: Installer must be a Super Admin or have Marketplace Access permission
Sensitive scopes and Enterprise-only scopes need an Enterprise account

gates.name: Private / unlisted distribution (before listing)
gates.unlocks: Other HubSpot accounts can install through your install URL without review, within caps.
limits: Private OAuth apps: 10 customer accounts by default, 100 if created in a Solutions Partner portal
Marketplace-distribution apps on platform 2025.2: capped at 25 installs until listed
Access tokens expire after 30 minutes; refresh with the refresh token
Listing minimum: at least 3 active unique unaffiliated installs
gates.time_to_reach: Same day for installs; listing prep takes days

gates.name: Marketplace listing, then certification
gates.unlocks: Listing removes the 25-install cap. Certification adds certified status.
limits: Listing: initial review within 10 business days; full feedback loop up to 60 days; one app under review at a time
Certification: listed 6+ months, 60+ active installs, security questionnaire, demo video, verified domain
Certification lasts two years, then must be renewed; a rejected app can reapply after six months
Error rate must stay under 5% of daily requests
gates.time_to_reach: Listing: weeks. Certification: at least six months after listing.

steps.title: Create a HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: Sign up for a HubSpot developer account, which is separate from a regular HubSpot account, and open the developer portal.

steps.title: Create the app and choose distribution
steps.detail: Create the app (UI or CLI). When asked, choose Marketplace distribution or restricted to specific accounts, and choose OAuth rather than a static token. Use OAuth because multi-account apps require it.
gotchas: Static-token apps work for a single account only, and can define only required scopes
Choosing Marketplace distribution on platform 2025.2 applies the 25-install cap until listing

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config and copy its callback URL
steps.detail: In Composio, create a HubSpot auth config using your own credentials and copy the callback URL it shows.
gotchas: Composio's callback path appears inconsistent between sources; use the one shown in your auth config

steps.title: Set the redirect URL
steps.detail: Add the callback to the redirect URLs in the app's auth config (app-hsmeta.json or the app's Auth settings).

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

steps.title: Declare scopes
steps.detail: List only scopes you use. Put feature-dependent scopes under conditionally required or optional. Avoid Enterprise-only scopes (e.g. crm.objects.custom.read) as required, since installs from lower tiers will fail.
gotchas: Composio's default list is long; trim it
Scope changes later require customers to reinstall or reauthorize

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret into Composio and install
steps.detail: Paste the client ID and client secret into the Composio auth config. Then connect your account with a Super Admin user, or use the install URL in the app's settings.
gotchas: Token requests send client_id and client_secret in the request body
Authorization codes are single-use and expire quickly

steps.title: Invite other accounts within caps
steps.detail: Share the install URL with customers or test accounts. Track the install count against the 10/100 private cap or the 25 marketplace-distribution cap. Switching from private to marketplace distribution later keeps existing installs.

steps.title: Request Sensitive Data scopes if needed
steps.detail: Private apps can add sensitive scopes in app-hsmeta.json. Marketplace-bound apps must request them from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team. The installing account must be Enterprise and a Super Admin must install.

steps.title: Prepare listing materials
steps.detail: Draft live Terms of Service and Privacy Policy pages, a public setup guide, a support contact, an install button URL, and a Shared data table matching your scopes. Make sure the URLs are crawlable by HubSpot's crawler.
gotchas: Need 3 active unique unaffiliated installs, with activity in the last 30 days
AI-connector apps must use user-level permissions or HubSpot's MCP server
Incomplete fields send the listing to Draft

steps.title: Submit the listing
steps.detail: Agree to the Technology Partner Program Agreement and submit one app only. Submitting a second while one is under review gets it rejected.

steps.title: Wait for listing review
steps.detail: HubSpot documents an initial review within 10 business days, and the full feedback loop should finish within 60 days of feedback. A third-party source reports 2-4 weeks (unverified).

steps.title: Apply for certification (optional)
steps.detail: After 6+ months listed and 60+ active installs, record a demo video (including disconnect and removal from Connected Apps), complete the security questionnaire, verify your domain, and call the Uninstall App API on removal.

requirements.item: Installer is Super Admin or has Marketplace Access
requirements.detail: Only these users can install apps. Reinstalls without new scopes do not need that permission.
Copy-pasting codes or tokens is prohibited for certification, and listing requires OAuth as the sole method.
Access tokens last 30 minutes; refresh via grant_type refresh_token.

Marketplace OAuth apps: 110 requests/10s per installing account per usage guidelines (the certification page says 100). Private apps: 100/app on Free/Starter and 190 on Pro/Enterprise. The limit-increase add-on does not raise Marketplace OAuth limits.
Extraneous scopes are rejected at certification.

scopes.effect: Added by default to all apps.
Enterprise-only; make it optional or conditionally required, or installs from lower tiers fail.
Sensitive Data scope. Marketplace apps must request access from the Ecosystem Quality team; private apps can add it in config. Needs an Enterprise installing account and a Super Admin.
Broad scopes in Composio's defaults; no HubSpot source labels their review category. Drop them if unused.

blockers.symptom: Install fails or the consent screen shows unexpected permission requirements
blockers.cause: The installer is not a Super Admin or lacks Marketplace Access, or a conditionally required scope is in the install URL for an account without the feature.
blockers.fix: Have a Super Admin install. Use tiered install URLs and move tier-specific scopes to optional.

blockers.cause: The 25-install cap on marketplace-distribution apps, or the 10/100 cap on private OAuth apps.
blockers.fix: Get the Marketplace listing approved to remove the 25 cap, or use a Solutions Partner portal for the 100 cap.

blockers.cause: Only one app can be under review at a time.
blockers.fix: Wait for the first review to finish.

blockers.cause: Incomplete or incorrect fields, or URLs not crawlable.
blockers.fix: Fix the fields and allowlist HubSpot's crawler user agent.

blockers.symptom: Scope change has no effect for existing users
blockers.cause: Existing tokens keep their original scopes.
blockers.fix: Ask customers to reinstall or reauthorize.

default_scopes: (and about 20 more; see the Composio toolkit)
composio.note: Start on Composio's managed app for testing and a quick start. Move to your own HubSpot developer app when you need your own client ID, your own consent screen, a Marketplace listing, or to avoid the shared app. Add Composio's callback as a redirect URL and trim the long default scope list, since listing and certification require minimal scopes.

open_questions: PKCE support is not stated in the token docs.
Whether the 25-install cap applies to unlisted apps created before 2025.2, or to MCP Auth apps, is unsettled.
No HubSpot page was found labeling non-Sensitive scopes as restricted for review.
Rate limit conflict: 110 vs 100 requests per 10 seconds.
Listing review timing: HubSpot says 10 business days initial; a third party claims 2-4 weeks.
Whether the developer account needs a paid plan or business verification, and the exact create-app UI flow, were not confirmed.
Composio's callback URI is inconsistent between sources; confirm it in your Composio auth config.
Refresh token lifetime is only described as long-lived.
Review timeline for the Sensitive Data request form is unknown.
